intro: Millwrights install, maintain and troubleshoot heavy machinery. The closest of the 25 careers below is aircraft structure and systems assembly, with an 84% skill match, while Boilermakers are 82% matched and earn a BLS May 2025 median of $76,410, which is 16% more than the $65,700 millwrights earn.
why_it_works: Setting up a production line means moving and leveling heavy equipment, aligning parts precisely and fixing what fails. O*NET rates equipment maintenance, installation and troubleshooting at 3.75 out of 5 for this job. Boilermaking, rail car repair and elevator work use the same skills. Several better-paid matches need a certificate or associate program. The gaps are equipment selection and operation.
tips: Elevator and Escalator Installers and Repairers earn $109,910, which is 67% more, through apprenticeships.
Mining roof bolters earn $78,540, or 20% more, with no extra schooling.
Transportation equipment electricians earn $84,890 if you add electrical training.

faq.q: What jobs can former millwrights do?
faq.a: The closest matches are aircraft structure and systems assemblers (84%), Boilermakers (82%) and Rail Car Repairers (81%), based on O*NET 31.0. Rail Car Repairers earn $67,530, which is 3% more than the $65,700 millwright median, and railroads train new hires.

faq.q: Which careers for millwrights pay more?
faq.a: 9 of the 25 matches pay more. Elevator installers earn $109,910 (67% more), transportation equipment electricians $84,890 (29% more) and mining roof bolters $78,540 (20% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Hydroelectric Plant Technicians earn $102,040 for their broader group.

faq.q: Do millwrights need more education to switch?
faq.a: Sometimes. 17 of the 25 matches need no more education than millwrights already have, including 6 of the top 10. In the closest match, 55% of workers have a high school diploma or the equivalent, while several electrical roles need a certificate.

The skills that most often need work are equipment selection, operation and control, operations monitoring and repairing. Operations monitoring already rates 3.62 out of 5 for millwrights in O*NET, so electrical controls and machine operation are the main steps toward better-paid trades.
